task.description: Independently validate TEST-DESIGNER's coverage of REQ-059's 8 acceptance criteria: at least one runnable test per AC, no skipped coverage, no TODOs, isolated/self-sufficient fixtures, no hardcoded secrets, and genuine (non-trivial) assertions. Specifically judge (1) whether the AC5 inspection-based source-split test is a legitimate way to verify the no-fallback guarantee or too fragile/gameable, and (2) whether the SUB_PROCESS/module_ref-unreachable-through-real-pipeline finding is a genuine out-of-scope gap rather than an excused coverage hole.
acceptance_criteria: AC1-AC8 each have >=1 runnable test, mapped in test/specs/REQ-059.md's coverage table
Fixtures use per-test unique data (Ecto.UUID.generate/System.unique_integer), no shared hardcoded IDs, no cross-test ordering dependency
Tests actually assert the right thing, not trivially passing
Judgment call on AC5's inspection-based test legitimacy
Judgment call on SUB_PROCESS/module_ref scope-boundary claim

result.summary:
Independently re-ran the suite (did not trust TEST-DESIGNER's report): `LETFLOW_DEV_DB_CONFIRMED=1 mix test test/letflow/engine/pin_resolver_test.exs test/letflow/engine_test.exs` -> 73 tests, 0 failures, real Postgres. `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` clean. All 8 REQ-059 ACs traced against docs/requirements.yaml's REQ-059 entry: each has >=1 non-trivial test (AC1 ordering+byte-identical Jason output via double resolve/4 call and equality assert; AC2 zero-row write verified by reading back instance_projections/instance_definition_snapshots/tokens/events counts, contrasted against a resolvable-pin case to prove causation; AC3 reuses REQ-024's JsonSchema.validate/2, asserts length(failures)==2 for a two-violation schema; AC4 reads the real INSTANCE_STARTED payload via Reconstruction.read_full_log/3 plus a migrations-directory grep proving no pin table exists; AC5 covered both behaviorally (pin_for/3 halt-on-first-unresolved with a counting lookup) and by inspection; AC6 threads two real Engine.create/2 instances with a real parent_instance_id, reads the child's real payload; AC7 uses an Agent-backed call-counting lookup proving the counter is unchanged after reconstruct_effective_pins/2; AC8 checked via a normalized_moduledoc/1 helper asserting ISS-0672/GH-306/S6/PLC-01 text). No @tag :skip, no 'TODO: implement test' (grepped both test files and the spec). No hardcoded secrets/connection strings (grepped). Fixtures are per-test unique (Ecto.UUID.generate/System.unique_integer([:positive,:monotonic]) throughout, matching this codebase's established convention) with no shared mutable state and no test depending on another having run first (each Engine.create/2 test provisions and tears down its own tenant schema).

Judgment call 1 (AC5 inspection test): legitimate, not excessive gaming risk. REQ-059's own AC5 text literally demands 'confirmed by inspection ... stated in the moduledoc' -- an inspection-based check is what the AC asks for, not a substitute dodging behavioral testing (behavioral halt-on-first-unresolved coverage exists separately, cases 5-7/23). Verified the three-pronged inspection is sound: (a) splits raw source at 'def merge_effective_pins(' and asserts nothing after that marker contains 'catalog_lookup'/'module_lookup' -- a rename of merge_effective_pins would fail the marker-presence assertion loudly (not silently pass), so this is fail-safe, not fail-open, against renames; (b) a whole-file regex count asserting exactly one `lookup.catalog_lookup` and one `lookup.module_lookup` occurrence -- confirmed directly against lib/letflow/engine/pin_resolver.ex (grep) that these two qualified references occur exactly once each, both inside resolve/4 (lines 268/270), matching the assertion; (c) a structural arity check that reconstruct_effective_pins/2 takes no Lookup.t() parameter at all. Residual theoretical gap noted but not disqualifying: a deliberately obfuscated rebind (e.g. destructuring `%Lookup{catalog_lookup: cl}` and calling `cl.()` under a different local name), or a wholly new catalog-access path bypassing the Lookup struct entirely, would not be caught by the substring checks. This is a known limitation of any textual-inspection test, not a defect in this one, and REVIEWER/SECURITY-REVIEWER already gated the actual implementation before TEST-DESIGNER wrote this; not grounds for FAIL.

Judgment call 2 (SUB_PROCESS/module_ref scope claim): confirmed genuine, not an excuse. Grepped lib/letflow/definitions/graph.ex directly: @node_type_map (line 203) has no 'SUB_PROCESS' key, and Graph.build (line 237) falls back to :unknown_node_type for any unmapped node_type_str -- so a real Definitions.create/2 JSON-graph path genuinely cannot produce a %Node{node_type: :SUB_PROCESS} today; that node type only exists in this codebase via a hand-built struct (as the pure-function tests correctly do at pin_resolver_test.exs's sub_process/2 helper) or via a future SUB_PROCESS-adding requirement (REQ-062, not yet merged per the task brief). This is a Graph-level gap strictly beneath REQ-059's own scope, not something REQ-059 introduces, and REQ-059's design doc already documents an adjacent SCOPE GAP (service_catalog/PLC-01) at the requirement level -- the test spec's honest inline note plus a comment in place of an unwritable integration test is the correct handling, not a hidden coverage hole. module_ref halt behavior remains fully covered at the pure-function level.

No issues found requiring rework.
